adminOnly: This setting is reserved for Admin users.

aiPolicies.title: AI policies and budgets
aiPolicies.description: Where client data may go and how much AI may cost each month.

policies.title: The four policies
policies.clients: {count, plural, =0 {No clients} one {# client} other {# clients}}
policies.external_allowed: Briefs, texts and images can be sent to the configured AI providers.
policies.external_restricted: Only providers approved for this client, with a confirmation before sending the client’s files.
policies.local_only: No data leaves the agency’s network; a configured local model is needed. Never falls back to the cloud.
policies.no_ai: No AI features for this client: templates, editor and exports by hand.

default.title: Default policy for new clients
default.hint: Applies to clients created from now on; existing clients keep theirs.
default.neverSet: Never changed: new clients start with external AI allowed.
default.label: Default policy

clients.title: Clients
clients.empty: No clients. The default policy will apply to the first client you create.
clients.name: Client
clients.budgetFor: Monthly budget of {name} in US dollars
clients.noClientLimit: No client limit: the agency budget applies
clients.changedCancelled: Policy changed. {count, plural, one {# waiting job was cancelled.} other {# waiting jobs were cancelled.}}
clients.localMissing: No local model is configured: AI features of clients with this policy will not start.

agency.title: Agency budget
agency.noBudget: No monthly budget: AI spending has no limit.
agency.label: Monthly budget (USD)
agency.hint: Leave empty for no limit. The limit carries over to the next months until you change it.
agency.forecast: At the current pace: {amount} by the end of the month
agency.thresholds: 70% · a warning to everyone · 100% · AI jobs do not start
agency.monthReset: The month is the calendar month in UTC; spending restarts on the 1st.

budget.alreadyExceeded: Budget saved. It is already exceeded: AI jobs will not start until next month.
budget.invalid: Enter an amount in dollars greater than zero, with at most two decimals.

smtp.title: Email (SMTP)
smtp.description: The email server Forgecy uses for sign-in links and invitations, read from the server’s .env file.
smtp.mailpit: Development environment: emails are caught by Mailpit and never reach real recipients. <link>Open Mailpit</link>

config.title: Configuration
config.missing: No SMTP server is set: sign-in by magic link is not available. Whoever manages the server sets SMTP_HOST and the other SMTP_* values in .env.
config.envHint: Values come from .env; changing them needs a restart of the web and worker containers.

test.title: Test email
test.lastOk: Last test on {date} by {name}: delivered to the server.
test.sent: Test email sent to {to}. Check the inbox and the spam folder.
test.failed: The test email was not sent. Check server, port, username and password in .env.

verify.ok: The SMTP server accepts the connection and the credentials.
verify.failed: The SMTP server cannot be reached or refuses the credentials.

dns.title: Domain authentication
dns.intro: So that sign-in links do not end up in spam, the sender’s domain needs these DNS records (your email service gives the exact values):
dns.spf: SPF: authorises the email service to send for your domain.
dns.dkim: DKIM: signs each message with a key published in DNS.
dns.dmarc: DMARC: tells receivers what to do with messages that fail SPF or DKIM.
dns.brevo: Suggested service: Brevo (free plan for low volumes). Any SMTP service works.

storage.title: Storage
storage.description: Where Forgecy keeps files and how much space they take. Moving files between storages is done from the command line.
storage.lowSpace: The disk is almost full (less than {percent}% free): uploads, renders, exports and backups may fail.

config.title: Configuration
config.envHint: Values come from .env; changing the driver needs a restart and moving the existing files.

test.ok: Write, read and delete succeeded in {ms} ms.
test.failed: The write test failed: check the folder permissions or the S3 credentials.

space.title: Space
space.s3Note: Space of the server’s disk; the S3 store’s space is managed by the S3 service.
space.unknown: Free space cannot be read on this system.

usage.title: Files by area
usage.truncated: Many files: totals count only the first 200,000.
